source.target: x86-64 Linux, WebAssembly i64 unsigned division/remainder; explicit zero-divisor traps
source.compiler_settings: Pinned Wasmtime 51.0.0-dev, speed_and_size; baseline/experimental built separately from identical WAT

contract.kind: same-WAT compiler A/B, bounded adjacent same-SSA-operands i64 udiv then urem to one two-result opcode, x86-64 only
contract.domain: unsigned 64-bit bit patterns, y!=0 with quotient/remainder; y==0 must trap. Derived second denominator (y+1) wraps and must trap when original y == UINT64_MAX
contract.signedness: unsigned division and remainder only; separately checked signed-division controls are out of scope
contract.overflow: 64-bit wrapping additions for derived operands, neither compiler is permitted to silently remove observable division traps
contract.poison_or_undefined: WebAssembly integer operations in selected fixtures have no admitted LLVM poison; machine-state flags, register liveness, and generic Cranelift pass safety are not globally proved
contract.comparison_scope: decoded x86-64 static instruction bytes and counts for each wasm function, not CLIF operation cost, whole-AOT size benefit, latency or throughput

qualification.independent_disassembly_and_aot_hash_che: all 14 contexts x both compilers; static instructions, divisions and decoded bytes recounted separately
qualification.guest_trap_code_and_wasm_origin_offset_a: passed for original same-WAT primary fixture, not a complete internal trap-map proof

two_live_pairs.comment: two independently derived quotient/remainder pairs; second denominator wrapping to zero remains a trap

exclusive_branches.comment: control case with quotient/remainder on mutually exclusive branches; experimental combiner made no change here

limitations: These are human-authored test contexts for an existing human-authored experimental pass, not new sequences discovered by the ZenoFCIS enumerator.

Finite original Wasmtime executions and independent native replays do not establish full 64-bit SMT proof, SSA/dominance/register-allocation correctness for arbitrary functions, flag/poison safety, or all-target correctness.
Compiler-pass and internal trap-table integrity require independent review; trap API and original-Wasm offsets were checked only for a narrow primary case.
Savings are static decoded x86-64 native instruction bytes; the whole AOT remains unchanged in these contexts, and representative runtime profitability is not established.
No Bytecode Alliance upstream PR or main/release branch mutation was made.
next: Prioritize compiler integration correctness (SSA/dominance/register-liveness/trap table), then representative workload profitability and a truly ZenoFCIS-discovered alternative before considering upstream submission.
